title: Using the Mobile Library Service
transcript:
Hello, everyone. I am the coordinator of the mobile library service, and I have been invited here to explain how it will work in your village. The vehicle will visit every other Wednesday. It is smaller than a permanent branch, but it connects to the same catalogue and offers more than the books you can see on its shelves.

The first stop will be beside the pharmacy, where there is enough room for the vehicle to park safely. We originally considered the school entrance, but the arrival time would have conflicted with buses collecting children. Please use the marked pedestrian approach rather than walking behind the vehicle.

You can register on your first visit. Bring proof of your address, such as a recent letter, and we will issue a library card. Existing cards from other branches remain valid, so there is no need to apply again. Children can join with a parent or another responsible adult.

The shelves will carry a changing selection of fiction, practical guides, and books for younger readers. If you want a particular title, place a reservation through the catalogue or ask the staff to do it for you. We will bring the item on a later visit and send a message when it is ready.

A small printer is available for documents such as travel tickets or application forms. Please bring the file on a memory stick or send it to the service email address before we arrive. We cannot guarantee that a large attachment will download quickly, because the mobile signal varies along the route.

Borrowing periods are adjusted to the visit schedule. If a public holiday causes a visit to be missed, the due date moves to the next planned stop. You will not receive a late fee simply because the vehicle did not come. You can also return items at any permanent branch when that is more convenient.

People who cannot reach the vehicle may nominate someone to collect books for them. Tell the coordinator in advance, so staff know who has permission. We can discuss other arrangements for residents with long-term mobility difficulties.

During the first three months, we will record how busy each stop is. This will help us decide whether the timetable needs longer visits or different times. It will not be used to remove a stop after one quiet afternoon. We know that a new service takes time to become part of people's routines.

questions.prompt: The vehicle will park beside the ____.
questions.explanation: 药房旁有安全停车空间，学校入口会与校车冲突。

questions.prompt: Readers can place a ____ for a specific book.
questions.explanation: 想借特定书籍可通过目录预约。

questions.prompt: A small ____ can be used for documents.
questions.explanation: 车上小打印机可打印票据或申请表。

questions.prompt: What happens when the service misses a visit because of a holiday?
options: All books must be returned to a permanent branch
The due date moves to the next scheduled visit
Readers must telephone to avoid a fine
questions.answer: The due date moves to the next scheduled visit
questions.explanation: 因假日停访会顺延到期日，不因车辆缺席而罚款。

questions.prompt: Why will usage be recorded initially?
options: To adjust visit lengths and times
To restrict borrowing in busy villages
To remove every stop with low attendance
questions.answer: To adjust visit lengths and times
questions.explanation: 统计用于调整停留时长或时段，不因一次人少就撤站。
